description.narrative:
OUTPUT 1: Government of Iraq is supported to facilitate energy transition in Iraq : INDICATORS: 1.1: # of national energy transition frameworks analyzed, debated and agreed by GoI. 1.2: # of NDC-aligned fiscal frameworks for Iraq analyzed and approved by GoI 1.3: # of grid-wide assessments completed on renewable energy (RE) absorption capacities. 1.4: # of NAMA finance-ready projects developed for Iraq.
OUTPUT 2: Improved knowledge and capacity of Iraq for transboundary water negotiations: INDICATORS: 2.1: # of multi-sectoral analysis conducted on Iraqi water needs, availability/supply and impact of water scarcity. 2.2: # of country specific guidelines produced to guide Iraqi negotiations team. 2.3: # of Iraqi officials trained on a) negotiation skills and b) laws and treaties on transboundary water basins management. 2.4: # of global platforms on transboundary water to which Iraq’s participation is facilitated. 2.5: # of legal framework/instruments developed to ensure Iraq’s compliance to the requirements of UN Water Conventions. 2.6: # of meetings held between Iraq and other riparian countries to review existing transboundary water treaties.
OUTPUT 3: Drought preparendess and risk reduction capacities strengthened in Iraq: INDICATORS: 3.1: # of Iraq Meteorological Service officials trained and to make better forecasts and early warning ( Data to be gender disaggregated). 3.2: National committee of early warning centers and user departments established and operationalized for dissemination of drought warning using multiple channels. 3.3: # of sectoral and provincial drought contingency plans based upon weather forecasts for a potential drought event. 3.4: # of farmers trained in/equipped for drought resilient technologies to minimize the impact on their livelihoods

1. Formulation of the Project Document and its approval by UNDP management: A project document (ProDoc) is mandatory for all UNDP projects in order to ensure effective project management. The Project Document is also essential to ensure transparency requirements. It includes the context, strategy, theory of change (including objectives, outputs, activities), workplan, M&E plan, risk matrix, budget, procurement plan and an HR plan. The ProDoc was prepared immediately upon signing of the Agreement with UK and following an internal review by the Local Project Appraisal Committee (LPAC), it was signed by the UNDP Resident Representative.
2. Project Inception: In order to mobilize national stakeholders for effective implementation, a project inception workshop was held on 13-14th February. The beneficiary ministries and departments were briefed about the project objective, results, activities, and other aspects. The participating entities included; the ministries of Environment, Finance, Planning, Water, Agriculture, Electricity, Transport (Iraq meteorology services), Kurdistan Environment Commission and the Directorate of Women Empowerment. Thirty-two (32) officials participated in the Inception Workshop. The stakeholders discussed the support the project would provide in the areas of NDC implementation, renewable energy/energy efficiency, water resources management and transboundary diplomacy, and drought early warning and preparedness capacity building.
3. Implementation of key activities: A set of launching activities was conducted under each output, mainly in the form of workshops and training and or participation in different for a. The workshops and training had diverse objectives; including capacity assessment, introducing best practices, sharing global experiences, technical skills development, and or planning for policy implementation. 277 government officials from different ministries and entities participated in the workshops, training and fora.
The recruited institutions and consultants are working on data collection, stakeholders consultations, analysis and the production of the outputs according to the ToRs. A Capacity Development for Iraq’s Water Diplomacy Workshop was help in March 2022. The goal of this in-person capacity building workshop was (i) to support senior Iraqi government officials and water specialists to effectively engaged in Water Diplomacy, and (ii) to advance transboundary water cooperation in accordance with international law, to enhance negotiations skills and negotiations capacity building and also implement IWRM at the transboundary level under SDG6 commitments.
A National and International Water Resource Management workshop was conducted in September 2022 to begin a process which enhances the Iraqi government’s capacity to manage water resources at home and abroad. GWH is in the process of designing the Multisectoral Analysis, collecting data and information to be fed to the Analysis.
RIMES help a training on early drought warming in March 2022 to build capacity of government stakeholders to increase drought preparedness and response. RIMES produced an institutional Assessment of Meteorological agency, Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Water Resources.
The recruited institutions and consultants are working on data collection, stakeholders consultations, analysis and the production of the outputs according to the ToRs.

The goal of this in-person capacity building workshop was (i) to support senior Iraqi government officials and water specialists to effectively engaged in Water Diplomacy, and (ii) to advance transboundary water cooperation in accordance with international law, to enhance negotiations skills and negotiations capacity building and also implement IWRM at the transboundary level under SDG6 commitments.
- A National and International Water Resource Management workshop was conducted in September 2022 to begin a process which enhances the Iraqi government’s capacity to manage water resources at home and abroad.

- RIMES held a training on early drought warming in March 2022 to build capacity of government stakeholders to increase drought preparedness and response. RIMES produced an institutional Assessment of Meteorological agency, Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Water Resources.
4. Procurement of services: The project got on board RCREEE to produce the grid assessment and energy transition framework, and an international consultant to develop a NAMA project. Two consultants – one internal and one national are working on the NDC fiscal modelling. The project recruited Geneva Water Hub to develop a Multisectoral water Analysis and together with international consultant improve transboundary water agenda of Iraq. One international consultant is working on supporting Iraq on IWRM. The project recruited RIMES to produce institutional assessment of early warning capacity of Iraq and establish an Early Warming Committee at the federal level. The project recruited WHH to increase drought preparedness and resilience of farming communities.
5. Project Board Meeting and the Project Approval: In order to seek endorsement of the Project stakeholders, the Project Board Meeting was held on 29th June in Baghdad. UNDP Resident Representative chaired the meeting, while the Minister for Environment represented the Government of Iraq. The ministries of Environment, Finance, Planning, Water, Agriculture, Electricity, Foreign Affairs participated in the meeting. Also, the Kurdistan Environment Commission attended the meeting. The Ministry of Education attended the meeting as an observer. Both the UK and Canada technical teams joined the meeting virtually. UNDP Project team briefed the meeting regarding functions of the Project Board. The Project team also presented an overview of the project, as well as the progress between January to June 2022. The Board members endorsed the project and requested for sharing the project documents. The requested documents were shared along the project board meeting minutes.
6. Project launch and related visibility activities : The project team also implemented numerous visibility activities. The Project launch was organized on 29th June, following the Project Board meeting. The Minister for Environment and ambassadors of UK and Canada along with the UNDP Resident Representative participated in the launch event and interacted with the Iraqi media. To go with the launch event, numerous visibility activities were conducted, including a press statement (carrying messages from UNDP, Ministry of Environment, UK and Canada), a video about the project was broadcasted to the media present at the event and social media posts were done.
